clue.text: What bounder did — arrogant upstart!

definitions.meaning: a bounder, read literally, is one who bounds, so what it did was leap into the air
describes someone risen above their station and puffed up about it

explanation.surface: A cad's behaviour is summed up in a sneer at a social climber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' is old British slang for a cad, which hides the literal reading: one who bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated adjective is a scornful word for a person who has risen socially and become conceited; the verb phrase means leapt.

clue.text: Close relations with America and the American government

parts.note: uncles are close family relations
AM is an abbreviation for America or American

explanation.surface: Family members keep close ties with the US and its administration.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure in the star-spangled top hat personifies the United States federal government.

clue.text: Crash as pilots read poetry

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters of the three words are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: Aircraft come down while their pilots are reading verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crash' rearranges ASPILOTSREAD, the letters of 'as pilots read'.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's epic poem is a celebrated work of verse, so poetry by example.

clue.text: The time to land is when it's not dark

parts.note: a day is a period of time
to light is to alight, to land on something

explanation.surface: Pilots are told to touch down only while it is still bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' is the verb: birds light on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Daylight is the natural light of day, the period without darkness.

clue.text: Shut up — long-serving Brownies are around

indicators.note: the word for the group of Brownies is placed around the word for long-serving

parts.note: Brownies, junior Guides, meet in a group called a pack

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for long-serving is read from bottom to top

parts.note: something long-serving is old

explanation.surface: Veteran Brownie leaders tell someone to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' turns OLD into DLO for this down entry. Brownies are the junior branch of the Girl Guides, organised in packs.
explanation.definitionFit: To padlock a door or gate is to lock it fast with a detachable lock.

clue.text: Old army man, one in the band

definitions.meaning: formerly the lowest commissioned officer in a cavalry troop, who carried the colours
a brass instrument like a small trumpet, or its player

explanation.surface: A retired soldier who now plays in a brass band.
explanation.definitionFit: The word named an obsolete cavalry officer rank and is also a valved brass instrument used in bands.

clue.text: In full flow, yet starts to appear uncertain

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, which here come into view

explanation.surface: A speaker in full flow suddenly looks unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something iffy is doubtful or dubious.

clue.text: Mollifies small number on board

indicators.note: to be on board is to be inside the ship, so the small number sits inside its letters

parts.note: SS is a steamship, a vessel one goes on board
wee is Scottish for small
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone calms a few passengers aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a crossword convention for going inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweeten someone is to soften or placate them, as mollifying does.

clue.text: Quite a lot of awe god created

indicators.note: what is created here is made new out of the letters of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A believer marvels at how much a revered deity has made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'created' rearranges OFAWEGOD, the letters of 'of awe god'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a fair number, a considerable quantity, despite its modest sound.

clue.text: To Mark, with love from Fingal O'Flahertie

indicators.note: 'with love from' reads as the letter love being taken from the name, not a sign-off

parts.note: Oscar Wilde's full name was Oscar Fingal O'Flahertie Wills Wilde, so his middle names point to his first name
love is zero in tennis scoring, hence the letter O

explanation.surface: A letter signed off affectionately to someone called Mark by Oscar Wilde.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the sign-off of a letter; 'from' takes O (love, a tennis zero) out of OSCAR, Wilde's first name, which the solver reaches through his middle names Fingal O'Flahertie.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark left on skin by a healed wound.

clue.text: Song of the good old days

definitions.meaning: a traditional song sung at New Year
the Scots title translates as 'old long since', times long past

explanation.surface: A request for a nostalgic tune about bygone times.
explanation.walkthrough: The Burns song sung at midnight on New Year's Eve has a Scots title meaning 'old long since', so it is both the song and the old days themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns's Hogmanay anthem has a title meaning times long past, so it names both a tune and bygone times.

clue.text: Publish plans if and when Soho's redeveloped

indicators.note: property that is redeveloped is rebuilt in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A developer announces plans in case the Soho district is rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redeveloped' rearranges ANDWHENSOHOS; 'if' is only a link. Soho is a district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: The card-playing idiom means to reveal one's intentions, making them known.

clue.text: Demanding a second card

parts.note: a king is a court card in a pack

explanation.surface: A card player insists on being dealt another card.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for something is requesting or requiring it, close to demanding.

clue.text: Fail to make any impression on Congress about reserve

annotationWithheld.why: 'Fail to make any impression on Congress about reserve' (CUT NO ICE): 'reserve' can give ICE and 'on' NO reversed, but no reading of 'Congress' gives the remaining CUT, and no search found the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Fail to make any impression on Congress about reserve

clue.text: Pardon house-breaking girl? On the contrary

indicators.note: the clue first says the girl breaks into the house, then reverses it so the house goes inside the girl

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name
a nest is a bird's house, its home

explanation.surface: A burglar girl asks to be let off, though the clue then flips who broke in.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the girl breaks into the house; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles, so the house goes inside the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is an official pardon granted to a group of offenders.

clue.text: In an emergency, put a listening device on the island

parts.note: a tap is a bug on a telephone line
inch is a Scottish and Irish word for a small island

explanation.surface: Spies plant a bug on an island during a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: Inch, from Gaelic, names small islands, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means if absolutely necessary, when hard pressed.

clue.text: Accountant warns partnership

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant
a driver hoots a horn to warn others

explanation.surface: A book-keeper alerts colleagues to a dubious business alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is a Chartered Accountant in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Used in the phrase 'in cahoots', the word means a secret partnership or collusion.

clue.text: In one of the branches, tea is an obsolete word

indicators.note: the tea and the is are placed in the word for a branch

parts.note: an arm is a branch, as of a tree or the armed services
cha is slang for tea
taken as written

explanation.surface: In some branch office tea is described with an old-fashioned word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branches' suggests trees or offices; an ARM is one branch of the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaism is a word no longer in common use, such as 'thou'.

clue.text: Rat? Count rat out

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A count is denounced as a rat and thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges COUNTRAT, the letters of 'Count rat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is slang for a traitor or deserter, one who changes sides.

clue.text: Writer and poet cut short by hanging

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: the poet's name loses its final letter, trimmed at the end

parts.note: Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: An author and a poet are executed by hanging before their time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the E from DANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant is a jewel that hangs from a chain; as an adjective it means suspended.

clue.text: In Spain, a burning car with four keys

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
D, A, F and E are four musical keys, named by their letters

explanation.surface: A Spanish car crash fire involving a vehicle with four ignition keys.
explanation.walkthrough: The keys are musical ones, each named by a letter; 'In Spain' places the definition, since the term is Portuguese/Spanish for the Inquisition's burnings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase meant an 'act of faith', the Inquisition's public sentencing and burning of heretics.

clue.text: A supporter washed up

parts.note: a shore is a prop or beam supporting a structure

explanation.surface: A fan is finished, their team out of the running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'washed up' looks like failure; it means landed on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Something washed up has been carried by the sea onto land.

clue.text: Express sorrow about the lady's fruit

indicators.note: the word for expressing sorrow goes around the pronoun for the lady

parts.note: to cry is to express sorrow
her is the possessive for a lady

explanation.surface: Someone mourns over a woman's fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The cherry is a small red stone fruit.

clue.text: Seeing end of fox that ate hen, I'd get upset

indicators.note: to get upset is to be overturned, so these letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A huntsman watches a hen-eating fox meet its end, and feels upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get upset' rearranges THATATEHENID, from 'that ate hen' and 'I'd'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hunting phrase means present when the hounds kill the quarry, so witnessing the finish.

clue.text: Item in individual's order

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words individual's order

explanation.surface: An entry in a person's list of instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item' looks like a noun; it is the old Latin adverb used in lists and wills to mean 'likewise'.
explanation.definitionFit: In inventories and wills, item was used to introduce each further entry, meaning likewise or moreover.

clue.text: County in which star makes a come-back

indicators.note: coming back means going in the opposite direction, so the word for the star is read from its end

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A celebrity performer returns to a provincial region.
explanation.walkthrough: Avon was an English county from 1974 to 1996, around Bristol and Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Avon was a former administrative county in south-west England.

clue.text: It's hard to start knitting about one row initially

indicators.note: the knitting phrase wraps around the letters for one and the start of row

parts.note: to cast on is to put the first stitches on the needle
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word row

explanation.surface: Beginning a knitting project around a single row proves difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: CAST ON is the knitting term for beginning; it goes 'about' I and R.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound adjective means rigid and unbreakable, as in a cast-iron guarantee, from the brittle metal.

clue.text: Showing diffidence, tiny boy has one short song for audience

indicators.note: for an audience means the built-up words are heard rather than read

parts.words: tiny boy has one short song
parts.note: Tiny Tim is the small boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol, giving TIM; one is I; a short song is a ditty

explanation.surface: A shy little lad with a single brief tune performs to listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: TIM, I and DITTY said together sound like the answer; Tiny Tim is the crippled boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Timidity is shyness or lack of confidence, the same as diffidence.
